message.content:
I don’t know how the system works under the hood—it’s not my job to worry about that. But I *do* know what matters to me as a dispatcher: the system needs to show me the **actual** route a drone is supposed to take, not just a list of waypoints.

Sometimes the system glitches and shows a route that doesn’t match what the drone’s actually flying. Last week, one of our inspection drones was supposed to go around a restricted zone, but the route it got was the old one—so it flew straight into a closure before we caught it. That’s why I always double-check the route *before* signing off, but if the system’s down or lagging, I can’t rely on it.

All I care about is that when I pull up a flight, I see:
- The **start and end points** (sites).
- The **exact path** it’s supposed to take (not just a list of points).
- Any **restrictions** along the way (closures, no-fly zones).

If the system stores it in a way that makes that hard to see or update, it’s just going to cause problems. And if it’s not fast—like when the system’s restarting or the network’s slow—it’s useless.
